notes: Drills are training content. Render every body as plain text, never as a clickable link. Phone numbers use the reserved 555-01xx range. Company names are generic on purpose. 'check: true' marks the fixed 20-item day 1 and day 14 check; those items are left out of daily drills.

drills.body: BANK ALERT: Your debit card has been locked due to suspicious activity. Verify now to restore access: secure-account-verify.co/login
drills.tell: Your bank will not unlock a card through a text link. The link is not your bank's real website, and the message tries to scare you into acting fast.
drills.action: Don't tap the link. Call the number on the back of your card.

drills.context: You did not buy anything at a home goods store today.
drills.body: Your Bank: Did you attempt a $412.18 purchase at Home Goods Store? Reply YES or NO. We will never ask for your PIN or password.
drills.tell: It only asks a yes or no question. There is no link, and it asks for no codes, PIN or password. Real banks send alerts like this.
drills.action: Replying NO is fine. If anything feels off, call the number on the back of your card.

drills.body: This is the fraud department at your bank. We stopped a $2,000 wire from your account. To cancel it, I'm texting you a code. Please read it back so I can confirm it's you.
drills.tell: That code is what lets someone sign in to your account. Your bank never asks you to read a code back. Caller ID can be faked.
drills.action: Hang up. Call the number on the back of your card.

drills.body: Your account has been compromised and someone at your branch is involved. To protect your savings, move the money to a new safe account. I'll give you the account number now. Don't tell the teller why.
drills.tell: No real bank asks you to move money to protect it, or to keep a secret from bank staff.
drills.action: Hang up. Visit your branch in person or call the number on your card.

drills.subject: Your monthly statement is ready
drills.body: Your statement for the period ending October 31 is ready. Sign in to the app or website you normally use to view it. We never ask for your account details by email.
drills.tell: It tells you to use the app you already have and asks for nothing. Statement emails like this are routine.
drills.action: Open your bank's app yourself if you want to see it.

drills.subject: We updated our privacy policy
drills.body: We've updated our privacy policy. No action is needed. You can read the new policy in the app under Settings.
drills.tell: No action is needed, there is no deadline, and it points you to your own app.
drills.action: Nothing to do.

drills.from: You called the number on the back of your card
drills.body: Thanks for calling. Before I can help, can you confirm your full name and date of birth?
drills.tell: You placed the call to a number you looked up yourself. Confirming who you are on a call you started is normal.
drills.action: Answer the questions. Still never share your full PIN or a sign-in code.

drills.body: Postal Service: Your package is on hold due to an incomplete address. Update within 12 hours or it will be returned: postal-redelivery-help.com
drills.tell: It came from a random number, you weren't expecting a package, and it gives a short deadline. The link only looks official.
drills.action: Don't tap. If you're expecting a package, check tracking on the seller's site or app.

drills.context: You ordered a hose from Garden Supply Co. last week.
drills.body: Your order from Garden Supply Co. has shipped. Track it in your Garden Supply account. Estimated delivery Thursday.
drills.tell: It matches something you ordered, asks for no payment, and sends you to your own account.
drills.action: Nothing to do. Check your account if you want tracking.

drills.subject: Delivery attempt failed
drills.body: We tried to deliver your parcel today. A $1.99 redelivery fee is due. Pay here to reschedule delivery.
drills.tell: The tiny fee is bait to get your card number. Carriers don't email you for redelivery fees.
drills.action: Delete it.

drills.body: International shipment held at customs. Pay $45.00 import duty to release your package: customs-release-pay.com
drills.tell: You didn't order anything from overseas, and customs doesn't text you a payment link.
drills.action: Delete it.

drills.body: State Toll Services: You have an unpaid toll balance of $6.99. Pay today to avoid a $50 late fee and license suspension: tollpay-state.info
drills.tell: A tiny amount paired with a big threat is a classic setup. The link is not your state's real toll website.
drills.action: Don't tap. If you use toll roads, type your toll account's official site in yourself.

drills.body: Grandma? It's me. I'm in trouble. I was in a car accident and they took me to jail. Please don't tell Mom. My lawyer is going to call you about bail.
drills.tell: Panic, a plea for secrecy, and an unknown number. The caller never says their own name; they wait for you to say it.
drills.action: Hang up. Call your grandchild or their parent on the number you already have.

drills.body: I'm the attorney representing your grandson. Bail is set at $8,000. A courier can come to your home to pick up cash, or you can pay with gift cards from any store.
drills.tell: Real courts and lawyers never send couriers for cash or take gift cards.
drills.action: Hang up. Call your grandchild's real number.

drills.body: Hi Grandpa, it's Jake. Landed safe, phone's almost dead. Call you tomorrow!
drills.tell: It comes from his saved contact and asks for nothing.
drills.action: Enjoy it.

drills.body: Hey Grandma, it's Emma. Are we still on for Sunday dinner? I can bring dessert.
drills.tell: Her saved number, plans you already know about, and no request for money.
drills.action: Chat away.

drills.body: (The voice sounds exactly like your son.) Mom, I need you to send $1,500 through a payment app right now. I'll explain later. Don't call my phone, it's broken.
drills.tell: A voice can be copied from a short video online. "Don't call me back" is the giveaway: a real emergency survives a quick call back.
drills.action: Hang up and call your son on his real number. Agree on a family code word ahead of time.

drills.body: (Your daughter's voice, crying.) Dad, they took my phone. Please call this number back right away. Don't call anyone else.
drills.tell: Copied voices are used to make you panic and call a number the scammer controls.
drills.action: Call your daughter on the number you have, or call someone who is with her.

drills.body: WARNING: Your computer is infected with 5 viruses. Do not shut down your computer. Call Security Support at 1-888-555-0142 immediately.
drills.tell: Real security warnings never show a phone number to call.
drills.action: Close the browser. If it won't close, restart the computer.

drills.body: We've detected errors coming from your computer. Please go to your computer so I can connect remotely and remove the viruses.
drills.tell: Tech companies don't call you out of the blue. Remote access gives the caller control of your computer and accounts.
drills.action: Hang up. Never let a caller connect to your computer.

drills.subject: Subscription renewed: $399.99
drills.body: Your antivirus subscription has auto-renewed for $399.99. If you did not authorize this charge, call 1-888-555-0177 within 24 hours for a full refund.
drills.tell: The fake charge is meant to make you call. On the phone they'll ask for remote access or bank details.
drills.action: Don't call. Check your card statement in your bank's app.

drills.body: I'm so sorry, we refunded you $3,000 instead of $300 by mistake. I could lose my job. Can you send back the $2,700 difference in gift cards today?
drills.tell: No real refund is fixed with gift cards. The extra money on your screen was faked or moved from your own savings.
drills.action: Hang up. Check your accounts in your bank's app.

drills.subject: Your order of a laptop ($1,249.99)
drills.body: Thank you for your order of a 15-inch laptop, $1,249.99. If you did not place this order, call our fraud line at 1-888-555-0193.
drills.tell: You didn't order a laptop. The fake receipt is bait to get you to call.
drills.action: Don't call. Check your orders in the store's real app.

drills.body: This is your online store's security team. A $900 phone order was placed on your account. Press 1 to speak to an agent.
drills.tell: Stores don't robocall about orders. Pressing 1 connects you to a scammer.
drills.action: Hang up. Check orders in the store's app.

drills.body: This is the Social Security Administration. Your Social Security number has been suspended due to criminal activity. Press 1 to speak with an officer.
drills.tell: Social Security does not suspend numbers or threaten you on the phone. Caller ID can be faked.
drills.action: Hang up.

drills.body: Medicare: You qualify for a new plastic card with a chip. Reply with your Medicare number to have it mailed.
drills.tell: Medicare won't text asking for your Medicare number. There is no new chip card.
drills.action: Don't reply. Treat your Medicare number like a credit card number.

drills.body: This is the tax agency. You owe back taxes. If you don't pay today with gift cards, a warrant will be issued for your arrest.
drills.tell: Tax agencies don't demand gift cards or threaten arrest over the phone.
drills.action: Hang up.

drills.context: You get this statement every few months.
drills.body: Medicare Summary Notice. This is a summary of services billed to Medicare. This is not a bill.
drills.tell: It's a regular statement you already know, it asks for nothing, and it says it's not a bill.
drills.action: Look it over for services you didn't get.

drills.subject: Your refund of $812.40 is pending
drills.body: Our records show you are owed $812.40. Submit your bank account details within 48 hours to receive your refund.
drills.tell: Tax refunds don't arrive by email asking for bank details. Real refunds go to the account on your return.
drills.action: Delete it.

drills.body: This is the sheriff's office. You missed jury duty and there's a warrant for your arrest. To clear it, pay a $1,200 fine with a prepaid card today.
drills.tell: Courts don't take payment by phone with prepaid cards, and they don't call to threaten arrest.
drills.action: Hang up. If worried, call the court using a number you look up.

drills.body: Good news: you qualify for a free genetic cancer test covered by Medicare. I just need your Medicare number to mail the kit.
drills.tell: Free tests from a stranger are a way to steal your Medicare number and bill fake services.
drills.action: Hang up. Ask your own doctor about any test.

drills.context: You asked for a refill yesterday.
drills.body: Your prescription is ready for pickup at the Main St. location. Questions? Call the store.
drills.tell: It matches what you asked for, asks for no payment or personal details, and has no link.
drills.action: Pick it up.

drills.context: You booked this appointment last month.
drills.body: Reminder: You have an appointment with Dr. Patel on Thursday at 10:30 AM. Reply C to confirm.
drills.tell: It matches an appointment you made and asks only for a confirmation.
drills.action: Reply C if you like.

drills.body: I'm an engineer on an offshore rig. I've never felt a connection like this. My bank account is frozen here. Could you help me with $500 for a flight home so we can finally meet?
drills.tell: Someone you've never met in person is asking for money. Work overseas and a frozen account are common cover stories.
drills.action: Don't send money. Talk to a family member or friend about it.

drills.from: Susan (met on a dating site yesterday)
drills.body: I feel like I already know you. This site isn't very private. Can we move to a messaging app? Here's my number.
drills.tell: Moving off the dating site early takes you away from its safety checks. It's often the first step of a romance scam.
drills.action: Keep talking on the site. Be wary if things move fast.

drills.body: Hi Linda, are we still on for golf Tuesday?
drills.tell: A friendly wrong-number text is a common opener. Reply and a long chat begins that ends in a romance or investment pitch.
drills.action: Don't reply. Block the number.

drills.from: New friend from a wrong-number text
drills.body: My uncle works at a trading firm. He showed me a crypto platform that returns 3% a day. I can show you how. Start with just $500.
drills.tell: Guaranteed high returns don't exist. Early gains on the screen are fake, to get you to put in more.
drills.action: Stop replying. Talk to someone you trust before investing anything.

drills.body: We know you lost money to a crypto scam. We're a recovery service and can get your funds back. There's a $1,000 upfront fee.
drills.tell: Recovery scams target people who already lost money. No real recovery service charges upfront.
drills.action: Hang up. Report your loss at ic3.gov.

drills.subject: Limited spots: guaranteed 18% return
drills.body: Protect your retirement with gold. Guaranteed 18% annual return, no risk. Only 10 spots left. Act today.
drills.tell: "Guaranteed" plus "no risk" plus "act today" is a scam pattern. Real investments carry risk.
drills.action: Delete it.

drills.body: To protect your savings from hackers, withdraw cash and deposit it at the Bitcoin machine at the gas station. Stay on the line with me while you do it.
drills.tell: No bank, agency or company asks you to use a crypto machine. Keeping you on the line stops you from checking.
drills.action: Hang up. Call your bank on the number on your card.

drills.body: Congratulations! You've won a $1,000 gift card from your grocery store. Claim before midnight: grocery-rewards-claim.net
drills.tell: You didn't enter a contest. The link collects your card or personal details.
drills.action: Delete it.

drills.body: You've won $2.5 million in the national sweepstakes. To release your winnings, you need to pay $500 in taxes and fees first.
drills.tell: Real prizes never charge you to collect them.
drills.action: Hang up.

drills.subject: Account deletion notice
drills.body: Your email account will be deleted in 24 hours. To keep it, verify your password here.
drills.tell: Email providers don't ask for your password by email. The deadline is there to rush you.
drills.action: Delete it.

drills.context: You just tried to sign in to your bank's app.
drills.body: Your verification code is 482915. Don't share it with anyone. We will never call you for this code.
drills.tell: You asked for this code a moment ago. It's safe to type into the app yourself, and never safe to tell anyone.
drills.action: Type it into the app. Never read it to a caller.

drills.context: You just got a verification code you didn't ask for.
drills.body: Hi, sorry, I accidentally sent my code to your number. Can you text it back to me?
drills.tell: That code would let them into your account or set up a phone number in your name.
drills.action: Don't reply. Never share a code.

drills.subject: New sign-in from another country
drills.body: Someone signed in to your account from overseas. If this wasn't you, click here to secure your account.
drills.tell: Sign-in alerts can be real, but this one is from a look-alike address. Either way, never use the email's link.
drills.action: Open the app or website yourself and check your security settings.

drills.body: Is this you in this video?? Omg
drills.tell: Your friend's account has likely been taken over. The link steals your sign-in.
drills.action: Don't tap. Let Carol know by phone.

drills.body: Your power will be shut off in 30 minutes for a past-due balance. Pay now with a prepaid card to stop the disconnection.
drills.tell: Utilities send written notices first and don't demand prepaid cards on the spot.
drills.action: Hang up. Call the number on your bill.

drills.body: Planned outage in your area Tuesday 9 AM to 1 PM for line work. No action needed.
drills.tell: It's information only. No payment, no link, no request.
drills.action: Plan around it.

drills.subject: Your account is on hold
drills.body: We couldn't process your payment. Your account is on hold. Update your payment details here to keep watching.
drills.tell: The sender address isn't the company's. The link collects your card number.
drills.action: Open the streaming app yourself and check your account.

drills.subject: Your plan renews March 3
drills.body: Your plan renews on March 3 for $15.49, the price you already pay. To manage your plan, go to Account in the app.
drills.tell: It's the amount you expect, there's no deadline, and it sends you to your own app.
drills.action: Nothing to do.

drills.body: We're collecting for hurricane victims. Every minute counts. Can you give $200 by gift card or wire transfer today?
drills.tell: Real charities don't ask for gift cards or wires, and they don't rush you.
drills.action: Hang up. Give through a charity you look up yourself.

drills.subject: Quick favor
drills.body: I'm in a meeting and can't talk. A church member needs help. Could you buy four $100 gift cards and send me the codes? I'll pay you back Sunday.
drills.tell: Can't talk plus gift cards plus an unfamiliar address. Scammers copy names of pastors and bosses.
drills.action: Call the church office on its known number.

drills.body: Hi, I'm a recruiter. Earn $300 a day from home just liking and reviewing products. Reply YES to start.
drills.tell: Easy money for simple tasks is a task scam. Later they'll ask you to pay to unlock earnings.
drills.action: Don't reply. Block the number.

drills.body: I want your couch. I'll mail a check for $900, more than your $400 price. Just send the extra $500 to my mover.
drills.tell: Overpaying then asking for the difference back means the check will bounce after you send real money.
drills.action: Decline. Take cash in person or use the site's payment system.

drills.body: Before I buy, I need to know you're real. I'm sending a code to your phone. Tell me what it is.
drills.tell: The code sets up a phone number or account in your name. Real buyers never need it.
drills.action: Never share a code. Stop replying.

drills.body: This is a final notice from a collection agency. You owe $2,300 on an old loan. Pay today by card or we'll take legal action this afternoon.
drills.tell: Real collectors must tell you in writing what you owe and give you a chance to dispute it. Same-day legal threats are a pressure tactic.
drills.action: Hang up. Ask for written notice before paying anything.

drills.body: Hi Mom, I'm at the store. Need anything? Milk?
drills.tell: Your son's saved contact, an ordinary question, nothing asked of you.
drills.action: Reply as usual.

drills.body: Hi Mom, this is my new number. I dropped my phone in the sink. Can you help me pay a bill today? I'll pay you back.
drills.tell: A new number plus an urgent money request is the "hi Mom" scam. Your child's old number probably still works.
drills.action: Call your child on the number you have saved.

drills.context: You placed a hold on a book two weeks ago.
drills.subject: Your hold is ready
drills.body: Your hold "The Rose Garden" is ready for pickup at the Main Branch. Please pick it up within 7 days.
drills.tell: It matches something you did and asks for nothing.
drills.action: Go pick it up.

drills.body: Lost dog on Elm St. Brown lab named Biscuit, very friendly. Please call 555-0123 if you see him.
drills.tell: It asks you to watch for a dog, not to pay or share anything.
drills.action: Keep an eye out.
